articleTitle: A dual band balanced planar inverted F antenna (PIFA) for mobile applications
publicationTitle: 2013 IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium (APSURSI)
abstract: A new low profile dual-band balanced planar inverted F antenna with meandered lines resonating in the 1800 MHz and 2100 MHz bands is proposed. The antenna size is 50 × 12 × 10mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> allowing it to be easily housed in mobile handsets. The return loss, radiation pattern, gain and current distribution of the proposed antenna is presented. Furthermore, agreement between simulations and measurements is shown for a balanced feed with zero phase difference. Then, the design with differential feeding is simulated for various feeding phase angles and the benefits of minimized current flow on the ground plane are highlighted.

articleTitle: Surface wave suppression properties of Perforated Artificial Impedance Surfaces
publicationTitle: 2013 IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium (APSURSI)
abstract: Surface wave suppression properties of Perforated Artificial Impedance Surfaces (PAIS) are investigated. It is shown that, by a proper choice of perforation geometry, surface wave propagation can be suppressed without the need of vias. This significantly decreases fabrication costs. It is also possible to overlap the surface wave suppression and reflection phase bands of the PAIS. Due to the rotational asymmetry of the structure, surface wave suppression is achieved in only one direction.

articleTitle: Discrete lens array optimization for MIMO communication
publicationTitle: 2013 IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium (APSURSI)
abstract: Continuous Aperture Phased MIMO (CAP-MIMO) is a novel transceiver architecture that combines the concept of beamspace MIMO and analog beamforming to fully exploit the advantages of high-dimensional MIMO channels with the lowest possible transceiver complexity. CAP-MIMO theory dictates that the analog beamformer affect a spatial Fourier transform. A CAP-MIMO prototype uses a discrete lens array (DLA) designed for broadside focusing, which approximates the Fourier transform well near broadside but degrades at larger angles. This paper discusses the optimization of the DLA to achieve a closer approximation to the Fourier transform over a wider angular spread. Numerical results obtained using an iterative algorithm are presented that demonstrate the more uniform performance achieved by the optimized DLA.

articleTitle: Layered RF phantom characterization for wireless medical vital sign monitors
publicationTitle: 2013 IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium (APSURSI)
abstract: Wearable antenna performance measurements were used to characterize a synthetic variable layered phantom testbed, representative of human tissue for operation in the 868/915 MHz, and 2400 MHz industrial, scientific and medical frequency bands. Antenna radiation efficiency measurements on the phantom were compared with measurements on the thorax region of a human test subject. The results show that the phantom is representative of the human body for the application of wireless vital sign monitors, where conductive connections are made to the tissue.

articleTitle: Electrically-small wearable textile antenna
publicationTitle: 2013 IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium (APSURSI)
abstract: This paper presents some preliminary results of a study on electrically-small wearable antennas, made of textile material, to be used in the low UHF band, around 860 MHz.

articleTitle: Design of an ultra-wideband reflectarray using transformation optics
publicationTitle: 2013 IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium (APSURSI)
abstract: Reflector antennas realized by reflectarrays have many attractive features that are unmatched by traditional reflectors. Low-profile planar reflectarrays can be made to have high gain and electronic beam steering. However, they tend to use elements operating near their resonant frequencies for achieving a large phase range, thus limiting their bandwidth significantly. Transformation optics (TO) offers a new way to design tunable reflecting devices while preserving many of the attractive features of a reflectarray antenna. The TO device accomplishes beam collimation by using a 2-D array of sub-wavelength dipoles, which is macroscopically seen as an effective medium, to incur different phase changes of the incident fields. The proposed reflector has a relative gain bandwidth of 150%.

articleTitle: Dual mode delta-patch antenna for short range wireless wearable device
publicationTitle: 2013 IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium (APSURSI)
abstract: We proposed a compact size planar dual band delt-apatch antenna in two layers of stacked PCB structure. The antenna supports two distinct operating modes at two different frequencies that a first mode of the antenna supports communication between multiple wearable devices on body and a second mode supports communication between wearable device to out body wireless network. The antenna design has been verified both in simulation and measurement to validate its operation at 950MHz and 2.4GHz bands.

articleTitle: Effects of absorbing layers on the RCS reduction and radiation performance of an antenna array
publicationTitle: 2013 IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium (APSURSI)
abstract: The benefits and drawbacks of employing a wideband absorber in the case of an array of slot antennas both on RCS reduction and radiation properties are investigated. The study will also address the RCS in case of oblique incidence.

articleTitle: Characterization of small specimens using an integrated computational/measurement technique
publicationTitle: 2013 IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium (APSURSI)
abstract: Traditional electromagnetic material property extraction techniques rely on the use of carefully chosen specimen and measurement geometries that have analytical solutions which relate material properties to scattering parameters. Specimens must be carefully formed into precise shapes to meet the geometrical requirements of the analytical solutions, which can sometimes be either difficult or impossible depending on the material. Here we present an extraction method based on the use of a computational, as opposed to analytical, solution which can be used with nearly any specimen geometry.

articleTitle: A simple method for image autofocusing in through-wall radar imaging
publicationTitle: 2013 IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium (APSURSI)
abstract: In practical applications of through wall radar imaging, the characteristics of the wall are usually unknown, which will defocus the image and displace the target from its true position. In this paper, a simple image autofocusing method is presented. This method employs only one search variable and a simplified focus measurement function, which can reduce the computation load of a real time radar system. The well-focused image in experiment validated the effectiveness of this method.

articleTitle: Higher-order mixed spectral element method for Maxwell eigenvalue problem
publicationTitle: 2013 IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium (APSURSI)
abstract: Conventional edge elements in solving vector Maxwell's equations by the finite element method will lead to the presence of spurious zero eigenvalues. Here we describes a higher order mixed spectral element method (mixed SEM) for the computation of two-dimensional TEz eigenvalue problem of Maxwell's equations. It utilizes Gauss-Lobatto-Legendre (GLL) polynomials as the basis functions in the finite-element framework with the weak divergence condition. It is shown that this method can suppress all spurious zero and nonzero modes and has spectral accuracy with analytic eigenvalues. Numerical results are given on homogeneous and doubly connected cavities to verify its merits.

articleTitle: Embedded UHF RFID tag antennas for automotive tire sensing
publicationTitle: 2013 IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium (APSURSI)
abstract: We present analysis and design optimization of passive UHF RFID (Radio Frequency Identification) tags for tracking automotive tires. The RFID tags are mounted on or embedded into tires to monitor their conditions, verify their history and track inventory. In this paper, we evaluated the performance of existing RFID tags designed specifically for tires. It is found that the current RFID tags do not operate well in the vicinity of adjacent tires. This is due to the tire's dielectric structure and metallic radial plies inside the sidewalls. These factors were also verified in simulation models. Recommendations for new tag designs will be provided at the meeting.

articleTitle: A subdomain adaptive integral method for arbitrarily shaped objects
publicationTitle: 2013 IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium (APSURSI)
abstract: A novel subdomain adaptive integral method (SAIM) is presented for fast analysis of electromagnetic radiation and scattering from three dimensional objects of arbitrary shape. In conventional AIM, a uniform Cartesian grid is built up to entirely enclose the object, and auxiliary point sources are used to efficiently calculate far-zone interactions. However, adopting one Cartesian grid will actually cause large amount of auxiliary point sources redundant for the far-zone interaction calculation. To reduce the excess of those redundant auxiliary point sources, in the proposed SAIM, the whole domain is divided into several subdomains and then each subdomain is properly enclosed in its smaller Cartesian grid. Furthermore, the current continuity boundary condition between adjacent subdomains is employed to ensure the accuracy. Compared with the conventional AIM, the proposed SAIM technique can significantly reduce the number of auxiliary point sources and improve the convergence of iterative process. Numerical examples show the accuracy and efficiency of the proposed technique.

articleTitle: Planar monopole antennas for the Brazilian Digital TV
publicationTitle: 2013 IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium (APSURSI)
abstract: This article analyzes three different monopole antennas for the use in the Brazilian Digital TV System (range from 479 to 773 MHz). Two low cost, planar monopole antennas were designed using a full wave electromagnetic solver and compared with an ordinary wire monopole. The scattering parameters were simulated and measured, as well as their behaviors when connected to digital TV tuners and to a spectrum analyzer, in an urban indoor environment.

articleTitle: Stability analysis of transmission lines loaded with non-Foster circuits
publicationTitle: 2013 IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium (APSURSI)
abstract: Superluminal waveguides periodically loaded with non-Foster circuits are investigated. Such systems are shown to have right half plane poles for the equivalent two-port scattering parameters for practical values of waveguide lengths consisting of many unit cells, and hence, they are unstable.

articleTitle: Scanning characteristics of a self-adapting phased-array antenna on a wedge-shaped conformal surface
publicationTitle: 2013 IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium (APSURSI)
abstract: The scanning characteristics of a linear five-element antenna array on a wedge-shaped conformal surface is investigated in this work. In particular, the half-power beamwidth (HPBW) of a self-adapting array is studied for various changing conformal surfaces. A general array factor expression is derived and used to compute the HPBW. From these results, the self-adapting limitations of the array are outlined. Finally, analytical computations are validated with measurements.

Author Keywords: Microstrip Array and Phased Array Antennas

articleTitle: Innovative 4G mobile phone LDS antenna module using plastronics integration scheme
publicationTitle: 2013 IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium (APSURSI)
abstract: An innovative LDS 4G antenna solution operating in the 698–960 MHz band is presented. It is composed of two radiating elements recombined in a single feed broadband antenna system using a diplexer. This circuit is realized thanks to lumped components, assembled directly on the plastic piece which supports the antenna. Corresponding measurements show a 260 MHz wide bandwidth (for S11@-6dB) and close results when diplexer integration is made onto FR4 PCB. It validates the plastronics integration scheme for innovative antenna module solutions.

articleTitle: Fluidic tuning of a frequency selective surface based on a four-arm Archimedean spiral
publicationTitle: 2013 IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium (APSURSI)
abstract: This paper investigates the effects of changing the superstrate above a sub-wavelength Archimedean spiral frequency selective surface. The first part of the paper outlines the design procedure taken to create the FSS geometry for both the band-pass and band-stop. The effects of adding a PDMS bonding layer and a fluidic channel layer above the FSS are investigated and the addition of these layers requires a retuning of the spiral topology. The final part of the paper discusses the effects of dynamically tuning the resonant frequency by changing the effective dielectric constant of the fluids in the superstrate.

articleTitle: EBG reflector-backed MIMO antenna with wideband isolation and uni-directional radiation pattern MIMO antenna for MIMO radar
publicationTitle: 2013 IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium (APSURSI)
abstract: Next generation multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) radar system poses challenges of requiring wideband, high gain, and multiple uncorrelated antennas for achieving better resolution than traditional phased array radar systems. A MIMO antenna with electromagnetic band-gap (EBG) reflector is developed for uni-directional radiation pattern. The wide in-phase bandwidth in EBG is thus necessary for wideband MIMO radar application. The spiral-like slot is placed between two antennas to cancel the transverse electric field component produced by the reflected wave from the reflector. The MIMO antenna achieves high isolation and stable uni-directional radiation pattern within C band (4-8 GHz) applications.

articleTitle: Ultra-wideband on-site coding receiver (OSCR) for digital beamforming applications
publicationTitle: 2013 IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium (APSURSI)
abstract: We present a novel low-cost reduced-hardware power efficient digital beamforming architecture suitable for wideband and large arrays. Particular to this realization is the introduction of an on-site code division multiplexing (CDM) technique at the analog front-end to significantly reduce the number of analog-to-digital converters (ADC). Concurrently, the number of parallel input/output (I/O) channels at the digital back-end are substantially reduced as well. This implies a corresponding reduction in the number of field-programmable gate arrays (FPGAs) for baseband processing as compared to conventional beamforming techniques. The impact of on-site coding on the overall signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) was evaluated and demonstrated that noise due to inter-channel interference (ICI) can be suppressed using brick-wall filters, high resolution ADC and orthogonal codes.

articleTitle: A broadband wide angle variable linear polarization rotator
publicationTitle: 2013 IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium (APSURSI)
abstract: A Ku-band wide angle variable linear polarization rotator with high cross-polarization discrimination (XPD) was designed, fabricated and measured. The rotator makes use of two 90° meanderline polarizers and a linear grid to perform the polarization rotation and cross-polarization suppression. The advantage of the present arrangement is that it requires only one rotating mechanism rather than the multiple mechanisms commonly required when only linear grids are used. Across the 90° angular range of rotation and for incidence angle up to 45°, the XPD is found to be better than 28 dB over a 20% frequency bandwidth.

articleTitle: A new compact multi resonance H-patch filtenna
publicationTitle: 2013 IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium (APSURSI)
abstract: In this paper, new compact H-slot patch microstrip filtenna configurations have been analyzed, investigated and optimized using the CST_MWS. The proposed H-slot patch filtenna has been mounted on FR-4 substrate having either full ground or defective ground with a single rectangular slot. Our filtenna configurations resonate at multi-frequencies of different narrowband and/or broadband. The presented filtenas are very simple structures and cover the 3G/4G wireless frequency band.

articleTitle: A multilevel out-of-core algorithm for FFT-accelerated time marching schemes
publicationTitle: 2013 IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium (APSURSI)
abstract: An out-of-core algorithm that reduces the main memory requirement of FFT-accelerated time-marching methods is proposed.

articleTitle: RF-emission device safety testing using MRI
publicationTitle: 2013 IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium (APSURSI)
abstract: Radiofrequency (RF) emitting wireless devices such as mobile phones are required to undergo standardized safety testing prior to entering the consumer market. Strict regulations are imposed on the amount of RF energy these devices are allowed to emit to prevent excessive deposition of RF energy into the body. In this work, a novel safety evaluation test for wireless devices using magnetic resonance thermometry is proposed.

articleTitle: Ultra-thin wideband absorbers comprised of Frequency Selective Surfaces with concentric square loop elements
publicationTitle: 2013 IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium (APSURSI)
abstract: An ultra-thin wideband Frequency Selective Surface (FSS) type absorber consisting of a double square loop with a center patch is proposed. The admittance of the FSS is engineered so that it exhibits a capacitive response within the frequency range of interest. The latter is below the substrate's λ/4 resonance, where the substrate is characterized by an inductive admittance. The two admittances cancel each other resulting in an almost zero input reactance. A -10dB return loss is achieved for normal incidence from 12-27 GHz.

articleTitle: An antenna-based RFID expansion joint monitor
publicationTitle: 2013 IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium (APSURSI)
abstract: We present the design and preliminary test results from an RFID-based sensor used for expansion joint gap monitoring. Discrete increments in gap length are related to a change in signal response of an array of RFID tags. We demonstrate that our sensor can be reliably used to monitor gap increments of 1 inch over a read distance of at least 0.5 m. Prospective design improvements and future research directions are also discussed.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic design optimization using mixed-parameter and multiobjective CMA-ES
publicationTitle: 2013 IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium (APSURSI)
abstract: In this paper, new variations of Covariance Matrix Adaptation Evolution Strategy (CMA-ES) are investigated for optimization of electromagnetic design problems. Two variations of the CMA-ES algorithm are presented: mixed-parameter CMA-ES and multiobjective CMA-ES. Examples and results are provided to evaluate the performance of these algorithms.

articleTitle: Considerations on a multi-user MIMO system using channel prediction based on an AR model
publicationTitle: 2013 IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium (APSURSI)
abstract: We consider a multi-user multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) system using block diagonalization and eigenbeam-space division multiplexing to suppress inter-user interference and inter-stream interference. In time-varying environments, the performance seriously degrades due to mistracking of beamforming. A channel prediction scheme can eliminate the effect of the time-varying environments. In this paper, using indoor measurement data, we evaluate the bit error rate (BER) performance of a multi-user MIMO system with channel prediction based on an autoregressive model. It is shown that the proposed channel prediction technique can improve the BER performance significantly.

articleTitle: Performing large full-wave simulations by means of a parallel MLFMA implementation
publicationTitle: 2013 IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium (APSURSI)
abstract: In this paper large full-wave simulations are performed using a parallel Multilevel Fast Multipole Algorithm (MLFMA) implementation. The data structures of the MLFMA-tree are partitioned according to the so-called hierarchical partitioning scheme, while the radiation patterns are partitioned in a blockwise way. To test the implementation of the algorithm, a full-wave simulation of a canonical example with more than 50 millions of unknowns has been performed.

articleTitle: A simple procedure for effective secret key sharing from wireless channel estimation
publicationTitle: 2013 IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium (APSURSI)
abstract: A procedure for effective secret key sharing from wireless channel estimation is presented. The feasibility of the bit sequence achieved after a proper decorrelation process is demonstrated by means of standard RNGs tests.

articleTitle: A beam steering compact patch antenna with high gain application
publicationTitle: 2013 IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium (APSURSI)
abstract: A beam steering compact patch antenna with high gain application is invented. The proposed antenna is capable to steer the beam radiation to 45°, 135°, 225° and 315°. This is realized in the unique form of single main radiator and four parasitic elements. The activation of the parasitic required a shorting pin to the ground that indicates ON state condition and the deactivation of the parasitic means no shorting pin to the ground that lead to OFF state configuration. Each of the shorting pins can be linked to the RF PIN diode switch. It is discovered in CST simulation software, the specified location of the pins is really significant to ensure the parasitic perform either as a reflector or director. Moreover, the proposed antenna has small physical dimension of 130 mm square. The simulation and measurement results have successfully exhibited the idea of the proposed antenna for smart antenna and WiMAX application.

articleTitle: Microwave imaging of breast tumors with contrast agents: Theoretical study of dielectric contrast enhancement requirements
publicationTitle: 2013 IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium (APSURSI)
abstract: We propose a microwave breast tumor imaging technique that exploits changes in tumor dielectric properties resulting from the use of a contrast agent. A linear system, whose solution is the agent-induced change in dielectric properties, is established based on a microwave inverse scattering formulation. The linear system is solved using a sparsity regularizer. We identify the minimum required increase in tumor dielectric properties introduced by a contrast agent such that a 1-cm-diameter tumor can be accurately localized in 3D realistic numerical breast phantoms across all breast density classes. The results may be used to guide future contrast agent development.

articleTitle: Fast estimate of thermal responses of biological bodies due to RF exposure
publicationTitle: 2013 IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium (APSURSI)
abstract: A fast approach is proposed for estimating the thermal responses of biological bodies due to RF exposures. The approach is based on ANN models. The results obtained from the fast approach agree well with those calculated directly from the thermal solver. The advantage is that the approach is fast and is not dependent on the biological body and mesh sizes.

articleTitle: Effective modeling of graphene as a conducting sheet in the Finite-Difference Time-Domain method
publicationTitle: 2013 IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium (APSURSI)
abstract: An effective approach for Finite-Difference Time-Domain modeling of graphene as a conducting sheet is presented. A novel technique for implementing a conducting sheet boundary condition in the FDTD method which is based on use of backward- and forward-difference schemes for the spatial derivatives is used for modeling of graphene sheet. Numerical examples are presented to show accuracy and applicability of the method.

articleTitle: An in-vivo wrap-around permittivity sensor for deep biological tissue monitoring
publicationTitle: 2013 IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium (APSURSI)
abstract: A new in-vivo wearable band sensor is introduced for continuous monitoring of the permittivity of biological tissues deep into the body. This sensor allows for identification of tissue abnormalities by measuring the tissue's permittivity. For medical applications, the sensor can be used to monitor the permittivity of lungs and presence of lung water as a precursor to congestive heart failure. The physical layout of the sensor allows for monitoring the same tissue from different angles.

articleTitle: Design a monopole antenna with three-tier small semicircles for ultra-wideband operation
publicationTitle: 2013 IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium (APSURSI)
abstract: This paper presents a monopole antenna with three-tier small semicircles for ultra-wideband operation. The monopole antenna with three-tier small semicircles which can get wider bandwidth is done by etching process on the FR4 substrate with 1.6mm in thickness and 4.4 relative permittivity. The ground plane is a semicircle with larger slit which is good for impedance matching. The S11 frequency response, radiation patterns, power gain, group delay, received pulse response, and phase change are also investigated. The relevant research reports can prove that a monopole antenna with three-tier small semicircles are very suitable for applications in ultra-wideband short-range wireless devices and apply to medical image.

articleTitle: A scaled experimental system for Underwater Seismic Imaging and exploration
publicationTitle: 2013 IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium (APSURSI)
abstract: Underwater Seismic Imaging (USI) is an acoustic technology that can provide the geographic information of seafloor and sub-seafloor. A laboratory sized scaled experiment system of the underwater seismic imaging system is designed and built to support the imaging and inversion algorithm research of USI. It integrates the fundamental electronic instruments and acoustic sensors with computer and basic control programs, can providing the ability of scaled USI experiments for real dimension as 2000 meters wide and 1500 meters depth, with real seismic frequency from 5Hz to 20Hz.

articleTitle: Gain enhancement using DOE lens and DNG lens
publicationTitle: 2013 IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium (APSURSI)
abstract: The present work investigates the feasibility of enhancing gain using two types of lenses. One is the Diffractive Optical Element (DOE) lens made of polystyrene, designed for 3 GHz. The second one is a dielectric double negative (DNG) lens [2] created by a triangular lattice of holes drilled in a high dielectric permittivity material to obtain a refractive index of -1 at 3 GHz. For both lenses beam focusing has been illustrated. Each of the lenses is placed in front of a radiating antenna, a slotted waveguide, and modeled in HFSS and CST. The results for beam focusing are very encouraging and work is in progress to show gain enhancement. Both types of lenses can be easily constructed and experimental measurements will be done to validate simulation results.

articleTitle: A low-cost dual-polarized wideband antenna
publicationTitle: 2013 IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium (APSURSI)
abstract: In this paper, a low-cost dual-polarized wideband base station antenna is presented. The antenna element can cover the frequency band from 1900 to 2700MHz. The results in this antenna design demonstrate that it is more cost-effective and can simplify the manufacturing process. The antenna consists of only one double-size PCB and two single-layer PCBs. It shows that the antenna element can provide more than 9dBi peak gain, 30dB isolation, 15dB co-cross polar ratio and preserve the symmetry of antenna pattern.

articleTitle: Novel multiband segmented dual-aperture-coupled annular ring microstrip patch for wireless router MIMO antenna system
publicationTitle: 2013 IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium (APSURSI)
abstract: In this paper, the novel multiband segmented dual-aperture coupled annular microstrip patch antenna is used as the radiating element in a 2×2 router MIMO system. The radiating element has two aperture coupling slots and the annular ring is segmented. The resulting antenna and MIMO system have omnidirectional radiation patterns with good broadside coverage for four frequency bands (1.85, 3.5, 4.55 and 5.6 GHz) spanning 3∶1 bandwidth. Polarization and pattern diversity are used to reduce correlation.

articleTitle: A plaster antenna for healthcare, telemedicine and disposable electronics
publicationTitle: 2013 IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium (APSURSI)
abstract: A small WIFI/Bluetooth low cost antenna based on a commercially available wash proof plaster and conductive textiles is developed for healthcare and telemedicine applications. The antenna shows good -10 dB reflection coefficient and radiation patterns performance in isolation as well as on the body. Furthermore, it lends itself to being rolled out and stuck on many surfaces, therefore further demonstrating the viability of using plaster strips for disposable electronics.

articleTitle: Effects of an inhomogeneous loop plate on tilted beam formation for a patch antenna
publicationTitle: 2013 IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium (APSURSI)
abstract: An inhomogeneous loop plate (iHomLP) is composed of M loops in the x-direction and (2N+1) loops in the y-direction. All the loops have the same peripheral length, and have different strip widths in the x-direction. It is found that, as the number of loops (2N+1) is increased, the gain increases gradually and reaches a maximum value. The frequency band of the VSWR is approximately 5.7% for M = 2N + 1 = 9.

articleTitle: Compact CPW fed ZOR antenna for WLAN application
publicationTitle: 2013 IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium (APSURSI)
abstract: A compact Zeroth Order Resonance (ZOR) antenna which can be used for 2.4 GHz WLAN applications is presented in this paper. The resonance of the structure is achieved by implanting a chip inductor in between the center conductor of an open ended coplanar waveguide transmission line and a short metal strip. As a result the total electrical size of the fabricated ZOR antenna is reduced by 0.096 λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub> × 0.08 λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub>. The reflection, radiation and the variation studies of the antenna are discussed in this paper.

articleTitle: Accelerating the Spectral Domain Moment Method for reflectarray's by two-orders of magnitude
publicationTitle: 2013 IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium (APSURSI)
abstract: The Spectral Domain Moment Method (SDMoM) as applied to reflectarray antennas is unique over that of the Space Domain Formulation in that the impedance matrix elements do not contain highly oscillatory exponential terms as they become absorbed in the transform definitions for the basis/testing functions when constructing the EFIE. Since a typical reflectarray contains thousands of elements and the design requires computation of a unique reflection phase curve for each, the computational demand is heavy. Understanding where these demands stem from allow development of methods to help alleviate, this paper both describes the root causes and provides remedies for each. When all remediation's are implemented, efficiency grows over two orders of magnitude as compared to that of the classical SDMoM.

articleTitle: Impact of sapling movements on VHF and UHF radio-wave propagations
publicationTitle: 2013 IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium (APSURSI)
abstract: In this paper, the impact of sapling movements on VHF and UHF radio channels is experimentally investigated in a tropical rainforest. The reported information is based on the analysis and modeling of continuous-wave (CW) envelope fading waveforms. It is found that the sapling movements can affect the radio-wave propagations and cause the variations on the received fields. Moreover, statistical analysis shows that the induced temporal variations can be conveniently modeled using a Rician distribution function. Its Rician K factor gradually decreases as the frequency increases or there are sapling movements.

articleTitle: Vlade MIMO antenna for the mobile phone
publicationTitle: 2013 IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium (APSURSI)
abstract: We designed a hybrid antenna using vlade technique for the mobile phone MIMO antenna. Two Monopole + IFA hybrid antennas are located upside and downside of the phone board. This antenna satisfies LTE700/CDMA/GSM/ DCS/PCS/ WCDMA bands within VSWR 3:1, and has 42.06 ~ 73.91% efficiencies over the desired band.

articleTitle: An agile reconfigurable beam antenna with nulling capability
publicationTitle: 2013 IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium (APSURSI)
abstract: We present a fully automated reconfigurable beam antenna with adaptive nulling capabilities. This antenna takes the form of an S-band eight-element phased array equipped with a digital beamforming electronic network that provides for instantaneous beam reconfiguration as well as nulling. We have fabricated a complete antenna system which exhibits promising test results. Demonstrated hardware performance confirms a successful assembly of subsystems that combine nulling techniques with both a digital beamforming principle and a beam reconfiguration algorithm.

articleTitle: Joint estimation of HRR and DOA for target recognition
publicationTitle: 2013 IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium (APSURSI)
abstract: Eigen-structure based technique is used to jointly estimate the direction of arrival (DOA) of a radar signal and the high range resolution (HRR) profile of a target as seen by a stepped-frequency radar. Real aircraft data is used to demonstrate the viability of the proposed method and a target recognition system is developed based on the extracted scattering information.

articleTitle: A 2D/3D RFID static test system developed in a spherical near-field antenna measurement chamber
publicationTitle: 2013 IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium (APSURSI)
abstract: This summary paper presents a method for evaluating radio frequency identification (RFID) readable ranges, implemented by integrating a spherical scanning antenna measurement system for RFID static tests in an anechoic chamber environment. RFID tags with either forward or reverse links dominated can be evaluated in the 2D and 3D measurement modes of the static test system.

articleTitle: Calculated results of stored electromagnetic energies and dissipated energies in the very small normal-mode helical antennas
publicationTitle: 2013 IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium (APSURSI)
abstract: Theoretical treatments of stored and dissipated energies of small antennas were made previously. In this paper, these energies are examined numerically through electromagnetic simulations. As study example, a normal-mode helical antenna is utilized. At the self-resonant conditions, stored electric and magnetic energies are shown to be the same value. And, dissipated energies that are consist of radiated and ohmic loss energies are shown to be equal to the input power. Moreover, dependencies to antenna structural changes are also studied.

articleTitle: Multi-scale structures analysis using automatic h-refinement and Discontinuous Galerkin Integral Equation
publicationTitle: 2013 IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium (APSURSI)
abstract: This work describes an automatic tool able to estimate the error in the Integral Equation solution in order to refine the mesh where the error is higher than the chosen threshold. The local refinement is performed through a hierarchical dyadic subdivision on the selected triangles to reach the desired error. As the resulting mesh is non-conformal, a Discontinous Galerkin scheme is applied.

articleTitle: THz impedance surface waveguides
publicationTitle: 2013 IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium (APSURSI)
abstract: A impedance waveguide working in the THz spectrum is studied. A high impedance (Z<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sub>) is surrounded by two lower impedance (Z<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>) surfaces. Total internal reflection is the requirement for the guidance and confinement of the waves in the waveguide. The waveguide model predicts the dispersion relation for the lowest five TM modes. The guiding channel is varied for different impedance ratios Z<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>:Z<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sub> of 1:10 and 1:3.

articleTitle: Gain improvement of phased arrays of small elements using spherical dielectric shells
publicationTitle: 2013 IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium (APSURSI)
abstract: Spherical dielectric shells are studied to improve the gain of arrays of compact elements at lower frequencies, where the distance between elements is much smaller than half wavelength. The formulations required to define the shell geometry are developed. Two and four element arrays are designed and simulated with and without shells to test the technique, and promising results are obtained at lower frequencies for the array with shells.

articleTitle: Physical-layer wireless security of reconfigurable antennas in line-of-sight channels
publicationTitle: 2013 IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium (APSURSI)
abstract: Secure transmission is one of the most important aspects of wireless communications systems. In contrast to traditional cryptographic methods, physical layer security exploits the propagation channel to ensure security. It has been proven that a time-varying reciprocal channel can be used to generate secret keys which are secure even when an eavesdropper is located near one of the communicating nodes [1]. For line-of-sight (LOS) and slow-fading channels, reconfigurable aperture (RECAP) antennas have demonstrated their utility for physical layer security [2].

articleTitle: A compact fourth-order unconditionally-stable four-stages split-step FDTD method
publicationTitle: 2013 IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium (APSURSI)
abstract: A compact fourth-order four-stages split-step finite-difference time-domain (SS4-FDTD) method is developed, that achieves higher computation efficiency than the previous original fourth-order SS4-FDTD by reducing the band-width of the system involved. From the stability and dispersion analysis, it can be concluded that the compact fourth-order SS4-FDTD method is also unconditionally-stable and has the same level of accuracy as the original fourth-order method.

articleTitle: Asymptotic solutions in the transition regions for scattered field by a conducting circular cylinder
publicationTitle: 2013 IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium (APSURSI)
abstract: We derive the asymptotic solutions for the scattering from a conducting circular cylinder applicable in each of the transition regions divided by the shadow boundary (SB) into the shadow and the lit side. The asymptotic solutions include an extended Pekeris caret function. We verify the continuity on the SB of the asymptotic shadow region solution and the asymptotic lit region solution. The validity of the asymptotic solutions derived here is confirmed by comparing with the exact solution.

articleTitle: A low profile antenna array for Customer Premise Equipment applications
publicationTitle: 2013 IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium (APSURSI)
abstract: A low profile antenna array designed for Customer Premise Equipment (CPE) at 800 MHz is studied in this paper. The antenna array consists of two L-shaped monopole antennas and a feeding network. By properly designing the phase and amplitude of the feeding network, a horizonal radiation beam that parallel with the ground plane was obtained. This design shows great potential for the directional and omnidirectional radiation switching applications.

articleTitle: Investigation of the effect of reflect array element periodicity on aperture efficiency
publicationTitle: 2013 IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium (APSURSI)
abstract: In this paper the effect of reflect array element periodicity on its aperture efficiency is investigated. It is shown that for a fixed aperture size the smaller the element periodicity is, the better the aperture efficiency will be.

articleTitle: Electrically-small eighth-mode SIW antenna with fixed frequency and independently tunable frequency
publicationTitle: 2013 IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium (APSURSI)
abstract: An electrically-small eighth-mode substrate integrated waveguide (EMSIW) antenna is presented for a dual-band operation. A low frequency of 1.575 GHz is constant for global positioning system (GPS) reception, while a high frequency of 2.4 GHz is electronically tuned for WLAN applications. The overall antenna size is miniaturized by introducing the EMSIW and the complementary split ring resonator (CSRR). The proposed antenna's performances are numerically and experimentally demonstrated from S-parameters and radiation patterns.

articleTitle: Circularly polarized array antenna composed of four open-loop elements
publicationTitle: 2013 IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium (APSURSI)
abstract: A circularly polarized array antenna composed of four open-loop elements is proposed for a CP beam scanning antenna. The array has a low-profile structure; the antenna height above the ground plane is small, 0.1 wavelength at 6 GHz. Analysis reveals that a scan angle range of 40° is obtained. The 3-dB reduction gain bandwidth is 27% (from 5.35 GHz to 7.0 GHz). Within this bandwidth, the axial ratio is less than 2 dB and the VSWR is less than 2.

articleTitle: Diakoptic FEM-MoM analysis using explicit connection between field and current bases
publicationTitle: 2013 IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium (APSURSI)
abstract: A diakoptic technique combining the finite element method (FEM) and the method of moments (MoM), and using dual sets of higher order basis functions is proposed for analysis of 3D electromagnetic radiation and scattering structures. These bases enable efficient modeling and significant reductions in the total number of unknowns, while satisfying the natural relation between curl-conforming and divergence-conforming quantities when closing the FEM domain by a MoM surface. The new diakoptic FEM-MoM technique is validated in an example of an array of 4×4 dielectrically coated spherical metallic scatterers.

articleTitle: Scattering of electromagnetic waves by an electrically short period subwavelength slot grating in a thick metal plate
publicationTitle: 2013 IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium (APSURSI)
abstract: This paper theoretically presents scattering characteristics of a TM electromagnetic plane wave of an electrically short period subwavelength slot grating in a thick metal plate, using mode matching technicque. The scattering characteristics are numerically calculated on the condition that the period is much shorter than a wavelength of the incident electromagnetic wave, and it is theoretically discussed about how the scattering characteristics can be controlled by changing the period.

articleTitle: A concentric-arrayed radial line slot array antenna for THz applications optimized using PSO algorithm
publicationTitle: 2013 IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium (APSURSI)
abstract: A concentric-arrayed radial line slot array (CA-RLSA) antenna is presented for THz (350 GHz) operation. This CA-RLSA antenna is optimized using particle swarm optimization (PSO) method. The PSO optimized THz antenna is demonstrated for five rows CA-RLSA. The final CA-RLSA antenna is delivering 24 dB gain, -44 dB cross-pol and has an axial ratio <; 1.5 dB.

articleTitle: Efficient evaluation of MoM reaction integrals for analysis of electrically large bodies of revolution
publicationTitle: 2013 IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium (APSURSI)
abstract: An efficient scheme is presented for the method of moments simulation of axially symmetric antennas. The formulation of the problem is briefly recalled, and the issues that arise in the evaluation of the reaction integrals are identified and solved. The bi-dimensional treatment of a three-dimensional problem allows us to analyze objects with a diameter equal to several tens of a wavelength in seconds. This feature is very important in antenna synthesis processes, where repeated full-wave simulations are needed.

articleTitle: Beam correction of a shared-arm dipole array for imaging radar applications
publicationTitle: 2013 IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium (APSURSI)
abstract: A 2-port shared-arm dipole array is designed and its beam pattern investigated. In designing a dipole array for near-field imaging, longitudinal arrangement of the elements may become a problem due to the antenna spacing limit for alias-free sampling. The proposed shared-arm dipole array is designed such that the two adjacent dipole elements share a single dipole arm, achieving an alias-free sampling in the aperture domain. In this paper, a simplified 2-port array is designed for a proof-of-concept. The beam pattern of the initial array with unloaded arms is shown to be tilted. The beam is corrected by resistively loading the arms.

articleTitle: Ground wave excitation by horizontal dipoles
publicationTitle: 2013 IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium (APSURSI)
abstract: Field expressions of ground wave excitation by horizontal electric dipoles (HED) that are elevated above a homogeneous earth are rigorously derived. Comparison is made with vertical electric dipole excitation. It is shown that the received fields of an HED feature a 1/ρ<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> decay in the far zone. The received fields increase with heights of the transmitting and receiving dipoles. Unlike the VED sources, the received fields of HED increase with the operating frequency.

articleTitle: Analysis of the signs of imaginary parts of the effective constitutive parameters in metamaterials
publicationTitle: 2013 IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium (APSURSI)
abstract: The resonance and antiresonance behavior of the effective parameters in dielectric composites consisting of array of dielectric spheres are investigated. By comparing the analytical solution based on Mie theory and Clausius-Mossotti relation with the full-wave analysis based on finite element method, it is shown that the negativeness of the imaginary part of the effective permittivity and permeability is a consequence of the coupling interactions between the induced electric and magnetic dipoles.

articleTitle: The finite element boundary integral method accelerated using a graphics processing unit
publicationTitle: 2013 IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium (APSURSI)
abstract: An implementation of the finite element boundary integral method with GPU accelerated code was developed to provide a significant improvement in computation time over the standard method.

articleTitle: A structured workflow for developing interoperable numerical analysis tools
publicationTitle: 2013 IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium (APSURSI)
abstract: Numerical methods have seen incredible progress in both research and development. While they are thought closely related, there is often a gap present in the progression between the two. This gap, here referred to as the Solver Research & Development Barrier (SRDB), is unfortunately large within the field of numerical solvers. A workflow is developed and presented to mitigate the effects of this barrier, and is intended to greatly extend the life cycle of research projects with minimal overhead.

articleTitle: Low-profile multimode antenna for vehicular applications
publicationTitle: 2013 IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium (APSURSI)
abstract: This paper presents a multimode antenna operating over the GSM, GPS and WIFI bands. The antenna exhibits an omnidirectional radiation diagram in the GSM band and a directive pattern at the GPS frequency. In addition, the proposed antenna has a low-profile, a solid structure and a reduced weight, which make it a good candidate for vehicular applications.

articleTitle: A differential CP measurement method
publicationTitle: 2013 IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium (APSURSI)
abstract: A high quality circularly polarized antenna is tested with linear polarizations in an anechoic chamber which features some unintentional multipath reflections. A differential measurement method is used to reduce the effects of the multipath and determine the circularly polarized patterns. The results are compared with measurements conducted in a high quality chamber.

articleTitle: Fast analysis and design solution of multi-antenna system for 1.15 to 5.825GHz mobile terminal applications with optimizing isolation performance
publicationTitle: 2013 IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium (APSURSI)
abstract: In this paper, Artificial Neural Network technique used for the analysis of multi-antenna system is presented. Used in conjunction with a developed Matlab code, this solution allows also to design quickly and accurately a high port to port isolation multi antenna system by giving the different physical parameters of the structure for desired performance set by the user for all application in the band of [1.15–5.825GHz]. Validated in this paper for a two-antenna system isolated by slot, this solution can be generalized to any other type of system.

articleTitle: Sectoral band-gap of planar corrugated surfaces by asymptotic corrugations boundary conditions
publicationTitle: 2013 IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium (APSURSI)
abstract: Electromagnetic bandgap (EBG) surfaces have customarily been defined as being prohibitive of surface-waves within frequency ranges called bandgaps, for all directions along the surface, this latter specification being an understood presumed condition and thus left out. However, not all practical applications require such an entire bandgap in terms of surface directions. Rather, there could be some situations where surface-waves are required to be suppressed along directions only within an angular sector but are instead desired towards others outside. This work investigates this aspect using planar corrugated surfaces as the vehicle for study, in virtue of its ease of surface-wave modal analysis of dispersion by asymptotic corrugations boundary conditions (ACBC).

articleTitle: Modulated leaky waves to mold the radiation from substrate integrated waveguide antennas
publicationTitle: 2013 IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium (APSURSI)
abstract: We present our latest results on leaky-wave antennas (LWAs) in substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) technology. It is demonstrated how the suitable tapering of the SIW dimensions allow to modulate the aperture fields induced by a leaky mode, and therefore to tailor the radiated field. Several illustrative beam-shaping examples operating at 15GHz are described, showing the flexibility of the used dispersion-driven synthesis technique, and the versatility of the proposed SIW technology.

articleTitle: Analysis of sparse trifilar array antenna
publicationTitle: 2013 IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium (APSURSI)
abstract: A sparse trifilar antenna can support two independent beams while, to reduce the interference between the beams, each array element supports only one beam. To minimize the grating lobe effects each beam is formed by three spiral arms resulting in a sparse random array arrangement. In this paper we investigate the impedance and radiation characteristics of such an array. We have shown that the active reflection coefficients are somewhat degraded in comparison to a fully populated array, however the directivity remains approximately the same, making the trifilar array a viable solution for multi-frequency, multi-beam communication applications.

articleTitle: Radial waveguide model for permittivity measurements of disk-shaped dielectric samples at RF frequencies
publicationTitle: 2013 IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium (APSURSI)
abstract: A new approach for measuring dielectric constants at RF frequencies (30-300MHz) is proposed. The proposed method utilizes the parallel plate test fixture and retrieves permittivity based on a radial waveguide mode. It is verified by simulation, and moderate accuracy (<;10%) is obtained. This method can be a complementary approach to other conventional ones which are available for lower or higher frequencies.

articleTitle: Evaluation of inter-cell interference suppression using tunable beam-width microstrip antenna in actual indoor environment
publicationTitle: 2013 IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium (APSURSI)
abstract: In this paper, we present the improvement method of the achievable rate using tunable beam-width microstrip antenna for the inter-cell interference (ICI) environment. 4×4 Multiple-Input Multiple-Output (MIMO) channels are measured in actual indoor environment by using tunable beam-width antennas at two across points. It is shown that the combination of the transmitting beamforming and beam-width control is effective in enhancing the date rate for the situation suffering from ICI.

articleTitle: On spurious resonant modes in the MOT solution of time domain EFIE
publicationTitle: 2013 IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium (APSURSI)
abstract: Theoretically, internal resonant modes should not be induced in the marching-on-in-time (MOT) solution of the time domain electric field integral equation since zero initial conditions are enforced at the beginning of time marching and the internal resonant modes do not satisfy these initial conditions. However, these spurious modes are always observed in the MOT solution. It has been conjectured in the past that numerical errors might establish the necessary initial conditions and allow the incident field to induce the internal resonant modes. Systematic numerical experiments carried out in this work prove this conjecture by demonstrating that the internal resonant modes' amplitudes are indeed dictated by the numerical errors and the spectrum of the incident field.

articleTitle: The integration of reconfigurable filters for the matching of wideband antennas
publicationTitle: 2013 IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium (APSURSI)
abstract: This paper presents a technique to reduce the cost and overcome the high processing power needed to analyze the signals received by wideband antennas. The idea is based on matching a wideband antenna to a reconfigurable filter. This will allow an easier processing for the received signal and the replacement of the bank of filters needed after the antenna by one reconfigurable filter element. Two prototypes are shown to prove the validity of the proposed technique.

articleTitle: Ultra wideband dielectric resonator antenna design
publicationTitle: 2013 IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium (APSURSI)
abstract: An ultra-wideband dielectric resonator antenna (DRA) is studied and investigated for wireless application. The dielectric resonator is fed by a microstrip line. The overall size of the proposed DR antenna is 20 × 35 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, and the thickness of the dielectric resonator is only 5.12 mm, which is suitable for mobile device. The design simulation is done by using computer simulation Technology Microwave studio suite 2012 (CST). The results represent that by using N-shaped dielectric resonator, a wideband impedance bandwidth of 111% for VSWR≤ 2 covering a frequency range from 3.59 to 12.61 GHz. A parametric study is presented.

articleTitle: Electrically small folded helix antennas for use as self-resonant, mesoband Hpm sources
publicationTitle: 2013 IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium (APSURSI)
abstract: We have previously considered the use of a modified, conical, folded helix antennas as the energy storage and radiation mechanism for an electrically-small, high power microwave (HPM) system. Our previous results allowed us to integrate the antenna with a HPM switch to achieve a resonance of below 40 MHz for an overall antenna dimension of 101.3 cm (ka = 0.42). In this paper, we consider other folded helix geometries in order to analyze the best one for compact, low-frequency HPM applications. The antennas were modeled using CST Microwave Studio, and each antenna type was evaluated for its resonant frequency, local field enhancement, and radiation properties.

articleTitle: A planar reconfigurable polarization antenna
publicationTitle: 2013 IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium (APSURSI)
abstract: A planar antenna with microsecond-reconfigurable polarization is described. The antenna consists of a sub-array of dual orthogonally fed elements, each rotated with respect to the other. The unique design improves circular polarization (CP) axial ratio and linear polarization (LP) performance. The antenna was fabricated and the measured results are presented, showing good LP (> 15dB) but poor CP (>0.3dB) rejection.

articleTitle: L-band LMS impairment mitigation by using diversity at the receiver
publicationTitle: 2013 IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium (APSURSI)
abstract: The results of a measurement campaign carried out to analyze the benefits of polarization and spatial diversity at the receiver for the L-band LMS propagation channel are presented. Polarization diversity measurements were carried out with a dual circular polarized antenna providing right-hand and left-hand circular polarization. Spatial diversity measurements were performed with two GPS antennas λ/2 apart. Satellite elevations within the range 1° to 80° in urban, suburban, rural, heavily wooded and lightly wooded environments were studied. Polarization diversity has showed to be the best option to reduce the effect of the deep fades.

articleTitle: Plasmonic photoconductive antennas for significant terahertz radiation enhancement
publicationTitle: 2013 IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium (APSURSI)
abstract: We present a novel photoconductive antenna which utilizes nanoscale plasmonic electrodes to significantly enhance the efficiency and terahertz radiation power of conventional photoconductive antennas. The terahertz radiation power enhancement results from a significant reduction in the average transport path of photocarriers to reach the device contact electrodes. Thus, the photocurrent levels feeding the terahertz antenna in a sub-picosecond timescale are considerably increased, resulting in significantly higher terahertz radiation power levels. By incorporating the nanoscale plasmonic electrodes into a photoconductive antenna, we experimentally demonstrate up to 50 times higher efficiencies and terahertz radiation powers, compared to a similar conventional photoconductive antenna without the plasmonic electrodes.

articleTitle: Robust antenna concept for RFID tag applications
publicationTitle: 2013 IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium (APSURSI)
abstract: The paper proposes an approach for immunizing the input impedance of a tag-antenna against disturbances by the proximity effect of external objects. The idea is to drive two symmetric closely-spaced antennas with out-of-phase excitations, resulting in a differential input impedance. When an object is placed in the close proximity of the antenna system, the coupling with the two symmetric antennas will be comparable over a wide range of angles around the array broadside. In such a coupling scenario the differential input impedance is maintained compared to its free-space value.

articleTitle: Enhanced radiation properties of spiral lens antennas
publicationTitle: 2013 IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium (APSURSI)
abstract: Spiral antennas have been widely used in the THz regime as ultra wide band-width feeds for dielectric lenses. Indeed, the impedance behavior of such antennas is very flat over the frequency band, especially when logarithm spirals are used. Even so, these feeds generate a relatively wide field inside the lens and this results into a poor illumination of the lens. In this contribution, we will demonstrate how the performances of these lens antennas can be considerably improved by using a small air gap between the spiral and the dielectric material.

articleTitle: Wave propagation in quasi-periodic particle chains
publicationTitle: 2013 IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium (APSURSI)
abstract: Almost periodic particle chains exhibit propagation properties that cannot be handled by the conventional tools that are usually applied to periodic chains.We present a mathematical framework for the analysis of such structures, and the modal features they posses. In particular, we show that guided modes exist as opposed to random structures where scattering must occur. Quasi-periodic chains are an important link between periodic and random structures.

articleTitle: Miniaturized thin soft surface structure using metallic strips with ledge edges
publicationTitle: 2013 IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium (APSURSI)
abstract: Thin soft surface of strips with ledge edges are used to reduce the strip period width and in turns a miniaturized structure is achieved. Numerical analyses are presented. A 20% relative bandwidth is achieved whereas a 10% bandwidth was achieved by using the conventional planar soft surface structure. The effect of via position was also studied in the proposed structure.

articleTitle: Re-visitation on the input impedance of two-arm frequency-independent antennas in free space
publicationTitle: 2013 IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium (APSURSI)
abstract: The proposed analytical close-form solutions for the input impedance of planar two-arm Archimedean spiral antenna in free space is a function of metallization ratio and can fulfill the Babinet's principle fundamentally. Therefore, the applications of proposed model to other planar frequency-independent (FI) antennas are examined and discussed in this paper. It is found that Archimedean and equiangular spiral can be truly FI antennas based on their geometric formulas, while log-periodic and sinuous antennas exhibit FI properties only at self-complementary structure. Measurements and numerical simulations of several FI antennas validate the statement.

articleTitle: Single-layer multiband ring microstrip antennas fed by a co-planar waveguide
publicationTitle: 2013 IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium (APSURSI)
abstract: This paper presents single-layer multiband microstrip antennas (MSAs) fed by a co-planar waveguide (CPW) for linear and circular polarizations (LP and CP). Multiple square ring MSAs with concentric arrangement are placed on the top surface of a dielectric substrate and are fed by a CPW formed on the back surface of the substrate. The ring MSAs can radiate LP at the respective resonant frequencies. In order to realize good impedance matching to the ring MSAs, tuning stubs are connected to the CPW under the ring MSAs, respectively. Therefore, this antenna serves as a LP multiband planar antenna. Furthermore, a CP multiband ring MSA is designed. In order to obtain good axial ratio characteristics, lateral and longitudinal widths of the ring MSAs with truncated corners are varied. In this paper, multiband performances with good radiation patterns as well as low cross polarization of the proposed antennas for LP and CP are demonstrated.

articleTitle: Optimization spatial multiple coil transmitter structure for wireless power transfer
publicationTitle: 2013 IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium (APSURSI)
abstract: The contactless charging system has a wide application range and many advantages for portable consumer electronic products. Wireless power transfer (WPT) includes both the transmitter and the receiver which are in the state of resonance to achieve high efficiency. This paper presents a new multiple overlapping coil transmitter structure which enables the receiver has high efficiency within transmitter center area in a freedom of movement manner. The optimization novel transmitter structure can achieve higher efficiency than the typical single coil. Simulation results show that the axial component of magnetic induction resulting from the overlapping coil structure has a preferable homogeneous distribution. The proposed optimization system achieves the efficiency of 60% for a receiver placed 10 cm away from a 4 coil (four overlapping coil) transmitter.

articleTitle: Frequency beam-scanning rhombic grid array antenna
publicationTitle: 2013 IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium (APSURSI)
abstract: A Kraus grid array antenna (K-GAA) and a rhombic grid array antenna (RGAA) are investigated as frequency beam-scanning antennas. The fundamental radiation characteristics, including the beam direction and gain, are discussed. The resonance for the RGAA is reduced by adding perturbation elements to the hexagonal loops, thereby enhancing the gain bandwidth.

articleTitle: A coaxial test fixture for transmission/reflection measurements of metamaterials
publicationTitle: 2013 IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium (APSURSI)
abstract: Metamaterial structures exhibiting negative permittivity and/or negative permeability have been given considerable attention in recent years, but limited discussion has been given to a standard way of measuring these structures. Often, metamaterial measurements involve cumbersome fabrication and setup procedures making it very difficult in some cases to generate accurate data because of noise in the system or the complexity of the setup. This paper presents the design of a test fixture that overcomes much of the difficulty in metamaterial measurements to provide quick and accurate data. Furthermore, the data generated from this test fixture can be used directly with current extraction routines to determine the effective properties associated with the metamaterial structure.

articleTitle: Combination of two neutralized coupling element antennas for low LTE and GSM mobile phones
publicationTitle: 2013 IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium (APSURSI)
abstract: An antenna-system covering the LTE700 and GSM850/900 standards is presented. The proposed structure has been designed to fit in generic handheld devices. It has been manufactured using Laser Direct Structuring technology on a plastic piece. The principal design challenge for the antenna is to cover the target band with a short ground plane (75mm). To be able to cover from low LTE (700–787MHz) up to GSM850/900 (824–960MHz) frequencies with this short ground plane, coupling element antennas are optimized in conjunction with matching networks. In this way, one of the antenna ports covers the low LTE standard, while the other port covers the GSM850/900 frequencies. To obtain an acceptable level of isolation between the antenna feeds, the neutralization technique is used. The proposed antenna was manufactured and the reflection coefficient and total efficiency measurements were performed, showing very promising and competitive performance.

articleTitle: Investigation of tumour detection using contrast agents and FEM-CSI in biomedical microwave tomography
publicationTitle: 2013 IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium (APSURSI)
abstract: A finite element contrast source inversion algorithm was used to invert synthetic contrast enhanced breast data in order to determine the location of tumours. Prior information about the anatomy and the electrical properties of the breast model, which is obtained by a blind inversion before adding the contrast agent, is incorporated in order to increase the likelihood of successfully locating the tumours. Simulating the use of a contrast agent by increasing the permittivity of the tumours allows for a positive detection of their position. This method was also applied to data obtained from a numerical human forearm phantom in order to show applicability to anatomical regions with varying homogeneity.

articleTitle: Multi-step Ka/Ka dichroic plate with rounded corners for NASA's 34m Beam Waveguide antenna
publicationTitle: 2013 IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium (APSURSI)
abstract: A multi-step Ka/Ka dichroic plate (Frequency Selective Surface (FSS)) is designed, manufactured and tested for use in NASA's Deep Space Network (DSN) 34m Beam Waveguide (BWG) antennas. The proposed design allows ease of manufacturing and ability to handle the increased transmit power (reflected off the FSS) of the DSN BWG antennas from 20kW to 100 kW. The dichroic is designed using HFSS and results agree well with measured data considering the manufacturing tolerances that could be achieved on the dichroic.

articleTitle: 60-GHz substrate integrated imaging guide leaky-wave antenna on LTCC
publicationTitle: 2013 IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium (APSURSI)
abstract: A substrate integrated image guide (SIIG) is proposed based on the low temperature co-fired ceramic (LTCC) technology. Compared with other existed structures, it is easier to design and better fabrication reliability is offered. It is shown that an SIIG has the lowest loss among various planar transmission lines in the V-band and thus it is considered as an excellent candidate for high-efficiency leaky-wave antenna designs. Two 60-GHz leaky-wave antennas including six uniform metal strips and nine-teen tapered elements are proposed and designed, respectively.

articleTitle: Dual-band cylindrical dielectric resonator antenna with varying permittivity in φ-direction
publicationTitle: 2013 IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium (APSURSI)
abstract: A dual-band cylindrical dielectric resonator antenna with varying permittivity in φ-direction for IEEE 802.11y and IEEE 802.11j systems fed by coaxial probe is proposed in this paper. The proposed structure is constructed using two different materials having different permittivites. In order to determine the performance of varying design parameters on resonance frequency and bandwidth, parametric study is performed by using the software HFSS. It is observed that the proposed structure resonates at two different frequencies at 3.68 GHz and 4.95 GHz. The proposed antenna can cover both bands of the IEEE 802.11y (3.65 GHz - 3.70 GHz) for Wi-Fi and IEEE 802.11j (4.90 GHz - 5.10 GHz) for the WLAN systems.

articleTitle: An enhanced mixed-form fast multipole algorithm using rotation methods
publicationTitle: 2013 IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium (APSURSI)
abstract: In this paper, the broadband accuracy of the mixed-form fast multipole algorithm (MF-FMA) is improved by applying rotation techniques. Two kinds of rotation methods are employed respectively. One is the coordinate system rotation technique. The other one is the pseudospectral projection based on fast Fourier transform (FFT). Either of them has certain advantages depending on the number of multipoles. Through rotation, translation matrices become very sparse, which enables us to save the storage as well as the CPU time. Hence, we can increase the number of multipoles in the low frequency regime to shift up the transition region of MF-FMA. The overall accuracy is thereby improved significantly.

articleTitle: A discontinuous Galerkin integral equation method for time-harmonic electromagnetic problems
publicationTitle: 2013 IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium (APSURSI)
abstract: We present a discontinuous Galerkin surface integral equation method, herein referred to as IEDG, for time harmonic electromagnetic wave scattering from non-penetrable targets. The proposed IEDG algorithm allows the implementation of the combined field integral equation (CFIE) using square-integrable, L<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, trial and test functions without any considerations of continuity requirements across element boundaries. Due to the local characteristics of L<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> basis functions, it is possible to employ non-conformal surface discretizations of the targets. Furthermore, it enables the possibility to mix different types of elements and employ different order of basis functions within the same discretization. Therefore, the proposed IEDG method is highly flexible to apply adaptation techniques. Numerical results are included to validate the accuracy and demonstrate the versatility of the proposed IEDG method.

articleTitle: UWB dielectric rod antennas
publicationTitle: 2013 IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium (APSURSI)
abstract: This paper reviews single-layer and multi-layer dielectric rod antenna design for ultra-wideband (UWB) applications. Different from “polyrod” antennas used for high gain over no more than an octave bandwidth, the UWB rod designs can have many octaves of bandwidth depending on the number of layers. The rod antennas discussed here were design to provide frequency-independent performance such as constant gain level, constant pattern, and constant phase center across the operating frequency band, not just impedance bandwidth.

articleTitle: A synthetic calibration technique for broadband applications using focusing antenna setups
publicationTitle: 2013 IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium (APSURSI)
abstract: This contribution describes a new calibration procedure, which is advantageous for broadband free space setups. This method is based on well-known self calibration techniques like thru-reflect-line (TRL). In contrast to the commonly used mechanical line standard the proposed procedure makes use of a synthetic line standard, which is realized by using different frequency points. Thus, the necessary shift of the electrical length is achieved by a shift of frequency instead of a shift of mechanical length. Hence, the synthetic calibration technique does not require any mechanical displacements of the setup. In addition, the number of measurements is reduced, since a separate measurement of the line standard is not required. This approach is verified by measurements and compared with conventional TRL calibration techniques.

articleTitle: Thinned printed technology phased array enhanced with Frequency Selective Surfaces for space applications
publicationTitle: 2013 IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium (APSURSI)
abstract: In this contribution we show how Frequency Selective Surfaces (FSS) superlayers can be used to improve the performances of the phased array antennas with large periodicities by achieving an angular filtering at the array element pattern level. We show the design of thinned 7×7 phased array in printed technology integrated with an inductive FSS. The array elements are dipole coupled slots placed at a distance of 2λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> of each other. As a reference benchmark we compare the performances of the 7×7 FSS based phased array with a 7×7 phased array composed of 2×2 sub-arrays. We show that an increase in the gain of more than 2.5dB is obtained in the FSS array with respect to the benchmark.

articleTitle: Gain enhancement by planar capacitive soft cavity at millimeter wave
publicationTitle: 2013 IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium (APSURSI)
abstract: In this paper, we propose to use a planar capacitive soft cavity, at millimeter wave, to enhance the gain of a cylindrical DRA. A 4 dB minimum gain enhancement is observed at 57 GHz. Even without superstrat, the cylindrical DRA have a minimum of 10.2 dB and a maximum of 11.2 dB over the whole ISM band (57GHz - 64GHz). The radiation pattern shows that the cavity is able to focus in one beam even when the DRA radiation pattern has two beams. This cavity can be used for beam steering/reconfigurable radiation pattern antenna. CST Simulations confirmed the principle of the gain improvement by the proposed capacitive soft cavity.

articleTitle: Basic performance of very large MIMO in small cell systems
publicationTitle: 2013 IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium (APSURSI)
abstract: Concept of very large MIMO (VL-MIMO) has recently been proposed. In this paper, basic performance of VL-MIMO is investigated when considering the small cell such as phantomcell. An optimal radio frequency which is suitable VL-MIMO is evaluated when changing the cell size in the phantomcell.
